epics.summary: Authentication & Access — Login and Registration APIs
epics.description: Epic covering the VWO login API and registration/signup API requirements from the API documentation and HLR. Foundation for all other features; dependency-first.

Epic covering VWO Testing: A/B, Split URL and Multivariate testing, SmartStats Bayesian engine, visual/code editors, goals, audience targeting, and real-time reporting. Derived from PRD section 4.1 and FR1-FR3, FR5-FR6.

Epic covering VWO Insights (heatmaps, session recordings, funnels, surveys) and Personalize (segmentation, real-time content), plus integration connectors. Derived from PRD sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.5 and FR4, FR7-FR8.

epics.summary: Enterprise Readiness — Security, Compliance, Integrations & Quality
epics.description: Epic covering non-functional requirements: performance (2s editing), security (2FA, RBAC, activity logs), data privacy (GDPR/CCPA), reliability (99.9% uptime), collaboration/workflow, and cross-device QA. Derived from PRD section 7 and FR9.

stories.summary: As a user, I want to log in to the VWO dashboard with valid credentials so that I can access my account and dashboard
stories.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc + HLR (Login).

POST https://app.vwo.com/login with {"username", "password", "remember", "recaptcha_response_field"}. Content-Type: application/json. No auth header.

Acceptance Criteria:
- POST /login with valid username+password returns 200/2xx
- Response includes user object: id, name, email, accountId
- Response includes account/policy flags (isActive, policy.ruleset)
- Response includes currentAccount.planType and productsEnabled
- User is redirected/able to access the dashboard
- Content-Type: application/json accepted; malformed body returns 4xx

stories.summary: As a user, I want to see a clear error when logging in with invalid credentials so that I know my login failed
stories.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc + HLR (Login).

Invalid email/password must return an error (no dashboard access).

Acceptance Criteria:
- POST /login with wrong password returns 401/error status
- POST /login with unknown email returns error
- Error response contains a meaningful message/code
- No session/token issued on failure
- Empty/missing username or password fields rejected with 4xx

stories.summary: As an API consumer, I want the login response schema validated so that integrations receive consistent, documented data
stories.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (Response - Validation).

Response JSON contract includes: id, name, email, accountId, isDemoAccount, shouldSeeOnboarding, isPasswordSet, isAccountVerified, policy {id, name, ruleset}, accounts[], currentAccount {id, timezone, isTrial, daysRemaining, isExpired, productsEnabled, planType, accountStatus, dataLocation}, isActive, createdOn, lastLogin, imageUrl, appVersion, twoFactorAuthenticationMethod, isSamlEnabled, proxyToken, playerToken.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Response matches documented JSON schema field-for-field
- policy.ruleset exposes canBrowse, canDesign, canPublish, isAdmin, isOwner booleans
- accounts[] present with id, name, isMainAccount, isAgencyAccount, isLinkedAccount
- currentAccount includes planType, productsEnabled (testing/deploy/data360), daysRemaining
- proxyToken and playerToken present on successful login
- Schema documented and versioned for API consumers

stories.summary: As a user, I want session and token handling (proxyToken, playerToken, cookies) so that I stay authenticated across API calls
stories.description:
Source: App VWO Login API doc (proxyToken, playerToken) + HLR verification dimensions (Auth, Cookie, Token).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Successful login returns proxyToken and playerToken
- Tokens are usable for subsequent authenticated API requests
- Session cookie (if any) is set and honored
- Remember flag persists session when true
- Token expiry/refresh behavior defined and handled
- Tokens are not logged or exposed in plaintext logs

stories.summary: As a user, I want to register/sign up so that I can create a new VWO account
stories.description:
Source: HLR (Registration section).

Registration API is the second API family in the HLR. Verification dimensions: URL, Payload, HTTP Method, Status, Request body, Response body, Header, Auth, Cookie, Token.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Registration endpoint is documented with URL and HTTP method
- Valid registration payload creates a new account
- Response body returns account/user details on success
- Duplicate/registered email returns an error
- Invalid/missing fields rejected with 4xx
- Header, Auth, Cookie, and Token behavior verified and documented

stories.summary: As a QA engineer, I want an API test matrix for login and registration covering headers, auth, cookies, and tokens so that API quality is verified
stories.description:
Source: HLR verification dimensions (URL, Payload, HTTP Method, Status, Request body, Response body, Header, Auth, Cookie, Token).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Test matrix exists for Login API covering all verification dimensions
- Test matrix exists for Registration API covering all verification dimensions
- Each row maps to a test case with expected status
- Header variations (Content-Type, User-Agent, Referer) covered
- Auth=none for login confirmed; cookie/token behavior asserted
- Matrix is versioned and linked to stories

stories.summary: As a product manager, I want to create and launch A/B tests with multiple variations so that I can validate UX hypotheses with empirical data
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 Experimentation & Testing; FR1 (Must); user flow 5.1.

Define hypothesis, target metrics, select audience segment, configure variations (visual/code editor), launch, monitor, review SmartStats results.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can define hypothesis and target metric
- User can create 2+ variations for a campaign
- Campaign can be launched and monitored
- Results conclude a winner via SmartStats
- Cross-device/cross-browser QA available
- Campaign scheduling supported

stories.summary: As a product manager, I want split URL testing so that I can compare experiences hosted on different URLs
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (Split URL Testing), FR1; HLR login context.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can define multiple URL variants for a split test
- Traffic is split deterministically across URLs
- Results reported per variant
- Split URL campaigns support goals and SmartStats

stories.summary: As a product manager, I want multivariate testing (MVT) so that I can test combinations of multiple element changes
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (Multivariate Testing), FR1.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can define multiple independent variables/sections
- System generates combination matrix automatically
- Results isolate contribution of each element
- MVT campaigns integrate with goals and reporting

stories.summary: As an analyst, I want the SmartStats Bayesian engine so that test results are statistically accurate and actionable
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (Bayesian-powered Intelligent stats engine - SmartStats); FR2 (Must); risks: data accuracy.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Results computed with Bayesian methodology
- Confidence/probability metrics shown per variation
- Results remain valid under low sample sizes
- Cross-tool validation integrations supported
- Report explains actionable conclusion (winner / keep running / inconclusive)

stories.summary: As an experiment creator, I want visual and code editors so that I can set up experiments as WYSIWYG or at developer level
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (version previews), FR3 (Must) - Visual & Code Editor; risk mitigation SDKs + docs + templates.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Visual (WYSIWYG) editor supports element editing without code
- Code editor supports custom JS/CSS for developer-level changes
- Changes preview before publish
- Editor supports versioning/revert
- Editing workflows respond within 2 seconds (PRD NFR)

stories.summary: As a growth manager, I want custom goals and metric configuration so that experiments align with business KPIs
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (Custom goals and metric configurations aligned with business KPIs); user flow 5.1 step 1.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can create custom goals (sign-ups, purchases, lead forms)
- Goals attach to campaigns
- Goal conversion is tracked and reported
- KPI alignment visible in reporting

stories.summary: As a marketer, I want audience targeting based on behaviors and attributes so that I can show experiments to the right segments
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (Audience targeting based on behaviors and attributes), FR5 (High).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Targeting by behavior (device, OS, traffic, visitor type) supported
- Targeting by attributes supported
- Saved segments reusable across campaigns
- Targeting rules applied at runtime correctly

stories.summary: As a product manager, I want real-time reporting and dashboards so that I can monitor experiment analytics up to date
stories.description:
Source: PRD FR6 (Must) - Real-time Reporting & Dashboards; success metrics (conversion %, velocity).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Dashboard shows live experiment status
- Conversion rate metrics displayed per variation
- Reports exportable (CSV/summary)
- Data refresh in near-real-time
- Reporting covers test outcomes and KPIs

stories.summary: As an analyst, I want heatmaps (click, scroll, focus) so that I can visualize user actions on key pages
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.2 Behavioral Insights (Heatmaps: click, scroll, focus), FR4 (Must).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Click heatmaps generated per page
- Scroll heatmaps generated per page
- Focus heatmaps generated per page
- Heatmap data correlates with device/segment filters
- Data visible in Insights dashboard

stories.summary: As an analyst, I want session recordings so that I can observe real user behavior and discover pain points
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.2 (Session recordings), FR4 (Must); use case discover pain points.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Session recordings captured for configured pages
- Recordings playable in dashboard
- Recordings filterable by segment/date
- Struggle behavior (rage clicks, etc.) surfaced if enabled
- Recordings retention policy respected (testingRetentionDays 90)

stories.summary: As an analyst, I want funnel analytics so that I can identify drop-off points in user journeys
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.2 (Funnel analytics to identify drop-off points); use case 5.2.

Acceptance Criteria:
- User can define funnel steps
- Drop-off % shown per step
- Funnel correlates with experiment outcomes
- Insights dashboard supports funnel visualization

stories.summary: As a UX researcher, I want on-page surveys and feedback so that I can collect qualitative input from visitors
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.2 (On-page surveys & feedback).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Survey templates creatable
- Surveys embeddable on-page
- Responses aggregated in Insights
- Survey targeting by segment supported

stories.summary: As a growth team member, I want the personalization engine so that I can deliver tailored experiences to segments in real time
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.3 Personalization, FR7 (High).

Segment by geography, behavior, demographics; deliver customized content in real-time.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Segmentation by geography, behavior, demographics supported
- Personalized content delivered in real-time
- Engagement of personalized campaigns tracked
- Personalization integrates with testing and reporting

stories.summary: As an engineer, I want integration connectors (Shopify, Salesforce, Segment, Snowflake) so that VWO data syncs with external platforms
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.5 Integrations, FR8 (High).

Shopify, Salesforce, Segment, Snowflake, WordPress, Drupal, CDPs and analytics systems, tracking & reporting tools.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Shopify connector works
- Salesforce connector works
- Segment connector works
- Snowflake connector works
- Connector auth/setup flows documented
- Data sync verified bidirectionally where applicable

stories.summary: As a user, I want editing workflows to respond within 2 seconds so that the platform feels responsive
stories.description:
Source: PRD section 7 Non-Functional (Performance: system responds within 2 seconds for editing workflows).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Editing workflows respond within 2 seconds (p95)
- Performance measured under representative load
- Slow endpoints identified and optimized
- Performance budget enforced in CI

stories.summary: As an admin, I want 2FA, role-based access control, and activity logs so that the platform is secure
stories.description:
Source: PRD section 7 Non-Functional (Security: 2FA, role-based access control, activity logs); login API flags (isTwoFactorAuthenticationEnabled, isSamlEnabled, twoFactorAuthenticationMethod).

Acceptance Criteria:
- 2FA enforcement configurable per account
- Role-based access control applied (Owner/Admin ruleset from login policy)
- Activity logs capture user actions
- Logs retained and queryable
- RBAC prevents unauthorized feature access

stories.summary: As a compliance officer, I want GDPR and CCPA compliance so that regional data policies are respected
stories.description:
Source: PRD section 7 Non-Functional (Data Privacy: GDPR, CCPA, regional data policies); login response dataLocation (AS01).

Acceptance Criteria:
- GDPR compliance requirements met
- CCPA compliance requirements met
- Regional data residency (dataLocation) honored
- Privacy policy/documentation updated
- Data deletion/export requests supported

stories.summary: As a platform owner, I want 99.9% uptime SLA so that enterprise customers can rely on the platform
stories.description:
Source: PRD section 7 Non-Functional (Reliability: 99.9% uptime SLA for enterprise customers).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Uptime SLA of 99.9% defined and measured
- Monitoring and alerting in place
- Incident response documented
- High visitor volumes handled without performance loss (Scalability)

stories.summary: As a team member, I want collaboration and workflow management so that my team can plan and track optimization initiatives
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.4 Program & Workflow Management, FR9 (Medium).

Central planning interface, collaboration tools for distributed teams, Kanban-style workflows for experiment backlogs.

Acceptance Criteria:
- Central planning interface available
- Collaboration tools support distributed teams
- Kanban-style backlog workflow supported
- Experiment backlog organized by status

stories.summary: As a QA engineer, I want cross-device/cross-browser QA and version previews so that experiments render correctly everywhere
stories.description:
Source: PRD 4.1 (version previews, cross-device/cross-browser QA); risk mitigation (SDKs + docs + templates).

Acceptance Criteria:
- Cross-device QA supported (desktop, mobile, tablet)
- Cross-browser QA supported (Chrome, Safari, Firefox, Edge)
- Version previews available before publish
- QA checklist integrated into campaign workflow
